/stan.name: Stan
/stan.title: Trader in training
/stan.goal: Become a top-tier day trader, one honest test at a time.
/stan.bio: Stan studies market history, sits a test on every year he has not seen, and keeps a journal of what his wins and losses teach him. He trades paper money until he earns real money.
principles: No emotions. Only rules and evidence.
Every loss gets written down and studied.
A result only counts on data I have never seen.
Beating a coin flip is not enough. I have to beat simply holding.
Protect the account first. Profit second.

/tasks.title: Turn prices into signals I can study
Learn the eras: bull, bear and sideways years
Sit an exam on every year I have not seen

/thoughts.text: Day one of school. No trades until I pass my exams. Let's study.
Heads up: this is practice data, not real market history. The numbers show how I work, not how real markets behave.
I have 30,240 days of prices across 8 stocks from practice data (demo), covering 14.5 years.
Built 28,224 study rows. Each one holds only what I could have known at that day's close. No peeking at tomorrow.

Lesson: I do worst when the stock is overbought (RSI over 70). Across 37 trades when the stock is overbought (RSI over 70), I won 32.4% with an average of -0.84% per trade. My overall win rate is 49.4%. Next step: trade smaller or stand aside in these conditions, then retest.

Lesson: I do best when volatility is rising. Across 75 trades when volatility is rising, I won 50.7% with an average of +0.03% per trade. My overall win rate is 49.4%. Next step: check this holds on new data before I lean on it.
Report card: on 10 unseen years I called direction right 51.3% of the time. Always guessing 'up' scores 50.8%, so my edge on direction is +0.5%.
Trading: 474 trades, won 49.4%, profit factor 0.832. $1 with me became $0.90. $1 simply held became $2.36.
I'm not ready to trade yet: I win fewer than half my trades; I lose more than I make; simply holding beat me. That's the honest result. I stay in school and work on my lessons.
